newsitem.title: JAPAN: Apple says to cut costs by $400 mln per year.
newsitem.headline: Apple says to cut costs by $400 mln per year.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc's chairman Gilbert Amelio told a news conference on Tuesday that the company will reduce costs by $400 million per year after restructuring measures are implemented.
The measures will be announced in March.
Amelio is in Japan to attend a four-day Macworld Expo in Tokyo.
Amelio said he would aim to streamline the company, but did not elaborate.
He said the firm would refocus its product priorities and seek to stabilise its business.
"The changes are about revitalisation and not about retrenchment (of Apple Computer)," he said.
Apple Japan Inc president Tetsuya Shiga said at the same conference that the Japanese unit did not plan to cut staff.
"I think we are short-staffed," Shiga said.
Apple stunned Wall Street last month with a $120 million loss in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, which ended in December, due to falling sales of its flagship Macintosh line.

Since then, the company has outlined a restructuring plan -- the second in 12 months -- that will involve layoffs to return the company to profits. Detailed restructuring measures will be unveiled next month.
